definitions.course: A self-contained, first-party learning programme published at learnmasterypath.com/<course>/ with its own syllabus, four progressive levels and lessons. One course is counted once, however many learning paths include it.
definitions.learning_level: One of four ordered stages of a course (Level 1 Entry/Foundation, Level 2 Intermediate, Level 3 Advanced, Level 4 Master), each with its own overview page.
definitions.module: One topic unit within a level. On Mastery Path each module is published as exactly one lesson page, so module and lesson counts are the same; module IDs record the level and position.
definitions.lesson: A published page under level-N/ that teaches one topic and is not a project or capstone (see 'project'). It counts as a qualifying lesson when it returns HTTP 200 and has at least the minimum number of words of published text.
definitions.exercise: A practice task inside a lesson, identified by a section heading that starts with Exercise, Exercises, Practice, Try it or Stretch goals. Counted on lessons only; practice sections on project pages are reported separately as project_exercise_sections. Not counted as lessons.
definitions.quiz: A module quiz is attached to one page (a lesson or a project) and has 3 to 8 questions (8 for merged lessons); a course's final quiz is one page of 18 to 24 questions plus coding challenges. Module quizzes, final quizzes, questions and challenges are reported separately and never counted as lessons.
definitions.project: A build task published as its own deliverable page whose file name follows the NN-project-… or NN-capstone-… convention. A teaching lesson whose slug happens to start with NN-project- (for example, project setup, project lifecycle basics or project recovery) remains a lesson when listed in rules.lesson_slug_exceptions. Projects are counted separately; never included in lesson counts.
definitions.capstone: The course-ending build: the Level 4 page whose file name is NN-capstone-… (exactly one per course, identified by name and level, not by position). Pages named NN-capstone-… in Levels 1-3 are level projects and are counted as projects. Capstones are counted separately from projects and from lessons.

classification.rule: Technology: the course teaches a programming language, software tool, platform, engineering or computing discipline. Professional development: the course teaches management, leadership, language, accounting/tax or marketing practice, even where software is used.

duplicate_reviews.by: AI-assisted content comparison at the owner's request
duplicate_reviews.note: Decision: not a duplicate. Compared both published course outlines and all 40 instructional Markdown pages in each repository (10 content pages per level; four level index/navigation pages excluded), including introductory lessons, advanced subject matter and final capstones. Independently checked the source Git trees: zero identical blob hashes across the 40 instructional pages. The page titles, objectives and worked deliverables address distinct professional disciplines. Product Management focuses on customer discovery, product requirements, prioritisation, roadmaps, experimentation, product strategy and product-organisation leadership; Project Management focuses on lifecycle, scope, schedule, budget, risk, procurement, delivery, program and PMO governance. Their overlapping management vocabulary reflects related professions, not the same course. This is an AI-assisted duplicate decision, not a human content review.
